synonyms: Heterotheca latifolia Buckley (treated by FNA at subspecies rank within H. subaxillaris)
look_here_first: Look for alternate, hairy and often glandular leaves; frequently subclasping upper leaves; branching yellow ray-and-disk flower heads. Inspect side of heads for glandular phyllaries and the coarse hairs at their tips; scent alone is unreliable.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Master Plant Pool row 552, My iNaturalist flora, 10 wild observations; source count 2
project_inclusion.range_basis: Native to Texas at state level per USDA GRIN; individual project target-zone county proof not audited

morphology_keys.habit: Aromatic, branching, taprooted annual or biennial; stem sparsely to densely spreading-hairy and glandular.
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate, lower leaves often petiolate and upper leaves sessile and sometimes partly clasping; variable ovate to lanceolate, toothed or nearly entire; check multiple mid and upper leaves.
morphology_keys.heads: Yellow ligulate ray florets and yellow tubular disk florets; side-view involucre with glandular and hairy phyllaries.
morphology_keys.subspecies: FNA separates subsp. subaxillaris by a terminal tuft of coarse hairs on outer/mid phyllaries (often 6–28) versus subsp. latifolia without distinct tuft (occasionally 1–2 hairs); geography and season matter.
morphology_keys.fruit: Ray and disk cypselae can differ; macro/microscopic examination for final polish.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Pluchea camphorata has non-yellow rayless pinkish/purplish heads; within Heterotheca verify upper leaf bases, vestiture, phyllaries and reproductive structures rather than flower color alone. Other Heterotheca comparison pending matched photo review.
